name: startup
description: Startup into full load, minimum load, and a protected near-short, all in one tran run
claim: README.md Target specification, 'Startup' row (DR-0004 amendment A9): monotonic into any load 0-50 mA, controlled ramp <=1V/ms, inside +/-2% within 3 ms of enable, overshoot <=+2%. Measured here for full load (~50 mA) and minimum/no external load. The third branch (near-short, 'startup into current limit') is evidence-only: a near-short is outside the ratified 0-50 mA load range and README.md's target table has no short-circuit-current row to check its peak against, so it carries no pass/fail checks. The DUT now instantiates Xilimit (issue #11 / PR #39, closed) and Xsoftstart (issue #38 / PR #44), so this is inrush into a PROTECTED near-short, unlike the unprotected-inrush framing of the pre-#39 record this one supersedes. Integration method: '.options method=gear' (tb_startup.spice header) -- ngspice's default trapezoidal integrator rings across the near-short branch's fast current-limit clamping and collapses the whole deck's global timestep, making this matrix unrunnable against the post-#39/#44 DUT (issue #48); Gear/BDF integration does not ring across that event. Not a tolerance relaxation -- reltol/abstol/vntol/chgtol stay at ngspice defaults -- but disclosed here per the sim/soft-start/ precedent for integrator-choice changes; see tb_startup.spice for the measured CPU cost and a same-corner sanity check against the (unaffected, still-trapezoidal) _full/_min branches. Update (#174, 2026-09-05, spec/decision-records/DR-0021): ldo_core's VREF was promoted from an internal net -- driven by Vref1, an ideal 1.2 V vsource instantiated INSIDE the subcircuit -- to a seventh top-level port, and the identical ideal source moved into this deck. No device was added, removed or resized, so this is an electrical no-op by construction: an ideal vsource is an ideal vsource wherever it is declared, its return was already the cell's VSS port, and it is an AC short to ground in both placements. It is not asserted on that argument alone -- origin/main at ec9e530 was extracted to a scratch tree and this bench was run on BOTH trees back to back, on the same host with the same ngspice and the same pinned PDK, and the per-corner measurement lines compared field by field; DR-0021's 'Evidence' section tabulates the result. Records minted from this deck before 2026-09-05 carry the pre-#174 six-port DUT netlist sha and are superseded on that ground alone, not because any number in them was wrong; per sim/README.md's append-only rule they are left untouched.
analyses: meas tran t_settle_full WHEN v(vout_full)=1.782 RISE=1 TD=1u
meas tran vpeak_full MAX v(vout_full) FROM=1u TO=6m
meas tran t_settle_min WHEN v(vout_min)=1.782 RISE=1 TD=1u
meas tran vpeak_min MAX v(vout_min) FROM=1u TO=6m
meas tran vpeak_short MAX v(vout_short) FROM=1u TO=6m
meas tran vfinal_short FIND v(vout_short) AT=6m
meas tran ipeak_short MAX i(vamm_short) FROM=1u TO=6m

operating_conditions.load_current: ~50 mA (Rload_full=36 Ohm), ~1 uA (Rload_min=1.8 MOhm, minimum/no external load), near-short (Rload_short=1 Ohm, protected by Xilimit -- see Claim)
operating_conditions.output_cap: 4.7 uF (DR-0001 window's upper bound, the softest/slowest startup corner) + 100 mOhm ESR, all three branches
operating_conditions.enable_state: EN steps 0 -> VIN at t=1us (1ns edges) for all three branches simultaneously
